# DropCap

A paragraph whose first letter is a large gold initial, made with CSS so the text stays one ordinary paragraph.

```tsx
import { DropCap } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- Once, at the start of a long text, to mark the entrance.

## When not to

- More than once per text, or on short texts: it stops marking a beginning.
- On a paragraph that starts with a number or a symbol.
- Inside a narrow column (under about 30 characters): the initial takes too much of the line.

## Examples

### First paragraph

One per text, at its start. Quotes and dashes before the first letter are taken into the initial by the browser.

```tsx
<div className="max-w-xl">
  <DropCap>
    Cuando abrió la puerta, la casa ya había empezado a hablar. Eran ruidos pequeños, de tablas que se acomodan y de agua que baja por las paredes, y ella los escuchó con la atención de quien aprende un idioma.
  </DropCap>
</div>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

## Accessibility

- **Assistive tech:** nothing is added or split: the paragraph reads exactly as written, because the initial is `::first-letter`, not a separate element.
- **Contrast:** the initial is 4.5:1 or better on the page (it is large text) in both modes.
- Opening quotes or dashes before the first letter are included in the initial by the browser.

## Content

- Start with a full word, not a single-letter word, so the initial is not read as a word of its own.

## Tokens

Component tokens, all aliasing semantic tokens (see [tokens.md](../tokens.md)). CSS variable = `--kafka-` + the path in kebab-case.

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `drop-cap.fg` | `{color.reading.dropcap}` |
| `drop-cap.padding-right` | `{space.8}` |
| `drop-cap.type` | `{typography.reading.dropcap}` |
